title: Did the music bring people together
summary: Hall and Gitler discuss integration, the dividing line of bop and the younger audiences.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: No, of course not. But, you know, it's always been said that -- and I've always felt this myself, you know, that this music has brought people together and shown, you know, how people can be together, and yet, on the other hand, a lot of times lip service is made to that, but right underneath it it still wasn't happening.
Well, this music is changing -- changing with our thinking and whatnot. Yes, it did bring people together at one point. Then when the -- the dividing line was when the bop era came about.
Yeah, I know. We talked about this to a certain extent before.

And so that carries on in our daily lives, because we speak about the jazz musicians and their progressing as far as employment goes. Well, those that are, say, of concert ability, names of concert ability, they don't help John Doe. They're rugged individualists. They're geniuses, all of them.
But as much as some people were put off by the boppers, and I'm not necessarily talking about the dope habits or anything like that, I'm talking about the

fact that a lot of the musicians who came out of that era, you know, decided they weren't going to be Uncle Toms, you know, and they were going to go straight ahead as people. You know, that did turn -- that would turn a bigot off for sure, because he would want, even if he was a polite bigot, he would want the, you know, the Uncle Tom -- power struggle Tom we were talking about.

But on the other hand, the younger people who came up in that era who were listening to music were brought together. I think a lot of whites and Blacks were brought together in the bebop period. Maybe a lot of the older people were turned off, but the people who came up together in that period were together at one point. I think maybe -- and something else happened again, you know, later on.
